leads.title: Bureaucratic oppression, the love of money and wealth that perishes ↔ Rivalry, time and the slanderer
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Riches kept by their owner to his hurt, lost in a bad venture, so that his son has nothing in hand (weight 6.3). Pair score 6.3.

Only in Bureaucratic oppression, the love of money and wealth that perishes: He will not much remember the days of his life because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart; When goods increase, those who eat them increase; the owner only sees them with his eyes; The profit of the land is for all; a king is for (served by) the cultivated field; Sweet is the sleep of the laborer whether he eats little or much, but the surfeit of the rich will not let him sleep; He who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver, nor he who loves abundance with income; If you see oppression of the poor in a province, do not be amazed: a high one watches over a high one, and higher ones over them; 'Naked I came from my mother's womb and naked I shall return there'; What profit (yitron) has a man from all his toil under the sun?; There is nothing better than to eat, drink and find enjoyment in one's toil; this is from the hand of God.

Only in Rivalry, time and the slanderer: Knowledge of certainty ('ilm al-yaqin) and the eye of certainty ('ayn al-yaqin): you will see hell; God's kindled fire rises over the hearts and is closed over them in extended columns; Oath by time or the afternoon (al-'asr): humankind is in loss; Rivalry in piling up (al-takathur) distracts people until they visit the graves; they will be asked about the pleasures; A fire is closed over the damned (mu'sada); Hell given proper names: Laza (scalp-stripper), Saqar (scorcher, leaves nothing), al-Hutama (the crusher), Hawiya (the abyss); Do not go about as a talebearer among your people; Woe to every slanderer and backbiter (humaza lumaza) who amasses and counts wealth, thinking it makes him immortal; Rhetorical formula 'And what will make you know what X is?' (wa ma adraka ma) introducing an eschatological term.

passages.text: יֵ֚שׁ רָעָ֣ה חוֹלָ֔ה רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ עֹ֛שֶׁר שָׁמ֥וּר לִבְעָלָ֖יו לְרָעָתֽוֹ
וְאָבַ֛ד הָעֹ֥שֶׁר הַה֖וּא בְּעִנְיַ֣ן רָ֑ע וְהוֹלִ֣יד בֵּ֔ן וְאֵ֥ין בְּיָד֖וֹ מְאֽוּמָה
כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר יָצָא֙ מִבֶּ֣טֶן אִמּ֔וֹ עָר֛וֹם יָשׁ֥וּב לָלֶ֖כֶת כְּשֶׁבָּ֑א וּמְא֨וּמָה֙ לֹא יִשָּׂ֣א בַעֲמָל֔וֹ שֶׁיֹּלֵ֖ךְ בְּיָדֽוֹ

leads.title: The vision on tablets; the righteous live by faith; five woes ↔ Rivalry, time and the slanderer
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Woe to every slanderer and backbiter (humaza lumaza) who amasses and counts wealth, thinking it makes him immortal (weight 5.6). Pair score 5.6.

Only in The vision on tablets; the righteous live by faith; five woes: The arrogant man's appetite is wide as Sheol and like Death never satisfied, gathering all nations; Woe to one who makes his neighbor drunk in order to gaze on his nakedness; The prophet stations himself on his watchpost to see what God will answer to his complaint; 'The righteous shall live by his faith (emunah)'; A series of 'woe' (hoy) taunt-sayings against an oppressor; The stone cries out from the wall and the beam answers from the woodwork; The vision is for an appointed time; though it tarry, wait for it, for it will surely come; Write the vision plainly on tablets so that a runner may read it; Woe to the one who says to wood 'Awake!' and to dumb stone 'Arise!'; there is no breath in it; The earth will be full of the knowledge of YHWH as the waters cover the sea; Peoples labor only for fire and nations weary themselves for nothing; 'Hush (has) before YHWH, all the earth', for he is in his holy temple or has roused himself; and 7 more.

Only in Rivalry, time and the slanderer: Knowledge of certainty ('ilm al-yaqin) and the eye of certainty ('ayn al-yaqin): you will see hell; God's kindled fire rises over the hearts and is closed over them in extended columns; Oath by time or the afternoon (al-'asr): humankind is in loss; Rivalry in piling up (al-takathur) distracts people until they visit the graves; they will be asked about the pleasures; A fire is closed over the damned (mu'sada); Riches kept by their owner to his hurt, lost in a bad venture, so that his son has nothing in hand; Hell given proper names: Laza (scalp-stripper), Saqar (scorcher, leaves nothing), al-Hutama (the crusher), Hawiya (the abyss); Do not go about as a talebearer among your people; Rhetorical formula 'And what will make you know what X is?' passages.text: וְאַף֙ כִּֽי הַיַּ֣יִן בּוֹגֵ֔ד גֶּ֥בֶר יָהִ֖יר וְלֹ֣א יִנְוֶ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֩ הִרְחִ֨יב כִּשְׁא֜וֹל נַפְשׁ֗וֹ וְה֤וּא כַמָּ֨וֶת֙ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׂבָּ֔ע וַיֶּאֱסֹ֤ף אֵלָיו֙ כָּל הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וַיִּקְבֹּ֥ץ אֵלָ֖יו כָּל הָעַמִּֽים
הֲלוֹא אֵ֣לֶּה כֻלָּ֗ם עָלָיו֙ מָשָׁ֣ל יִשָּׂ֔אוּ וּמְלִיצָ֖ה חִיד֣וֹת ל֑וֹ וְיֹאמַ֗ר ה֚וֹי הַמַּרְבֶּ֣ה לֹּא ל֔וֹ עַד מָתַ֕י וּמַכְבִּ֥יד עָלָ֖יו עַבְטִֽיט
